written.myAnswer: Raising the temperature of a liquid makes its molecules move more vigorously and increases its internal energy.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
Heat is energy transferred from one body to another because of a temperature difference.
Heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature.
Heat is energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference. Internal energy is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of a body's molecules.
Energy travels from your hand, at a higher temperature, to the colder surface.
The statement is correct: a body has internal energy, while heat is energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference.
